attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's finding against the matrix R7 shipped, and it is R7's own XOR vacuity reappearing inside the artifact R7 built to diagnose it. `conserved` is =, `attenuates` is ≤, `extends` is ⊇ — all reflexive — so `before == after` satisfies capability ⊇, objectives =, authority ≤, evidence ⊇, world ⊇ and lineage ⊇ while externalizing nothing. check-mosaic.mjs §10 now SIMULATES the no-op against every row and reports that 2 of 6 (externalize-capability, fork-agent) are satisfied entirely by it; both are rejected by a strict effect (`strictly_extends` on support_realization and on lineage). `reset` is the one obligation a no-op violates, which is why the other four rows were never exposed. Operation = precondition + effect + conservation.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, on ROUND7_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md. The shape is Hoare-triple: a specification with only an invariant and no postcondition admits skip. Within this ledger it is the fourth appearance of `the rule checked the form of what was written, not the presence of what was owed`.

attrs.review_focus: The check is that a row with no `reset` cell is satisfied by before==after. That is a property of the six obligation kinds as defined here; a different vocabulary with an irreflexive conservation relation would not have the hole.
attrs.statement: A conservation matrix cannot define the operation it conserves around: every conservation relation is reflexive, so a total no-op satisfies an entire row, and an operation must therefore carry a precondition and an EFFECT with a strictly irreflexive required change.
